label: D2C skincare
brief: A premium skincare brand selling a small range of clinically-backed serums direct to consumers. Our customers are in their 30s and 40s, have tried a lot of products that did not work, and are sceptical of marketing claims. Every ingredient is disclosed with its concentration. We want first-time visitors to buy the starter set.

brief.product: Clinically-backed serums (small range) sold as a starter set
brief.audience: Sceptical skincare buyers in their 30s and 40s
brief.priceContext: Premium pricing justified by clinical backing and ingredient transparency

heroStrategy.question: Which hero strategy will best move a first-time visitor toward the primary conversion action?

ranked.label: Credibility is the main thing standing between the visitor and the action; lead with proof others trust it
The product needs to be explained before anyone will act; a clear headline and benefit statement lead
Seeing the product work is the most convincing argument; lead with a visual or interactive demonstration
Visitors already know what they want; putting the core tool or search directly in the hero beats persuasion

ctaStrategy.question: What should the primary call to action ask the visitor to do?

ranked.label: Ask for the core conversion action immediately — the visitor is ready
Ask the visitor to browse or discover first; the decision needs more input
Ask for a low-commitment trial or free tier before asking for money
Ask the visitor to talk to a person; the purchase is considered, high-value or bespoke

socialProofType.question: Which form of social proof will carry the most weight with this audience?

ranked.label: Named individual quotes; the audience responds to human stories
Aggregate star ratings and review counts; consumer purchase with many alternatives
Hard numbers — users, volume, ratings; the audience responds to scale
Recognisable company names; the audience is professional and judges by peers

contentHierarchy.question: What should the page lead with after the hero, given how this audience makes decisions?

ranked.label: Lead with benefits, proof and objection handling — the visitor needs convincing
Lead with what the product does and how to use it — function over feeling
Lead with browsing, inspiration and options — the visitor is still choosing

visualDirection.question: Which visual register best matches this brand and audience?

ranked.label: Monospace accents, fine borders, restrained palette — reads as built for experts
Neutral, dense, efficient — reads as a reliable tool
Generous spacing, imagery-led, magazine-like — reads as inviting and considered
High contrast, strong type, saturated accent — reads as decisive and modern

pageArchitecture.question: How much page does this product need to make its case?

ranked.label: A conventional mid-length page covering features, proof and pricing
A long page — the decision is complex and needs features, comparison, FAQ and objection handling
A short page — hero, proof, one CTA. More would dilute a simple decision

navigationComplexity.question: How much navigation does this page need for the visitor to feel oriented without being distracted from the primary action?
levels: Almost none — a wordmark and a single action; anything more competes with conversion
Moderate — a few destinations plus the primary action
Full — multiple sections and categories; the visitor genuinely needs to navigate

ranked.label: Moderate — a few destinations plus the primary action
Almost none — a wordmark and a single action; anything more competes with conversion
Full — multiple sections and categories; the visitor genuinely needs to navigate

interactionDensity.question: How interactive should this page be for this audience and product?
levels: Static and editorial — reading, not operating; interaction would be noise
Some interactive affordances — tabs, toggles, a few controls that aid the decision
Heavily interactive — the page should behave like the product itself

ranked.label: Some interactive affordances — tabs, toggles, a few controls that aid the decision
Static and editorial — reading, not operating; interaction would be noise
Heavily interactive — the page should behave like the product itself

offerProminence.question: How prominent should price, offers or commercial terms be on this page?
levels: Absent — price is not how this decision is made, or is not public
Present but secondary — available for those who look, not leading
Leading — price or offer is the strongest argument and belongs high on the page

ranked.label: Present but secondary — available for those who look, not leading
Absent — price is not how this decision is made, or is not public
Leading — price or offer is the strongest argument and belongs high on the page

trustIsPrimaryBarrier.question: Is trust or credibility the main thing preventing this audience from converting?

audienceIsPriceSensitive.question: Is this audience primarily motivated by price?

requiresEducation.question: Does the visitor need to be taught something before the offer makes sense?
